# A unit interpolated bare, compiled and run as Go, then run again on the
# interpreter. The assertions are on the strings themselves, so the two
# runners have to produce the same text and not merely both succeed.
#
# testdata/unit_bare_display.txtar says what the three targets generate; this
# says the generated Go builds and answers, and that `sngl test` on its own
# default platform answers the same. That pairing is the claim this class of
# bug needs: bare display was never asserted anywhere, so one program had a
# different answer on each of five paths and every one of them exited 0.
#
# `over` is the case that needs both runners the most. Go carried a duration
# as a time.Duration and handed its String out, which normalises across units
# -- so 500ms printed `500ms` and agreed with the interpreter by coincidence,
# while 1100ms printed `1.1s` and did not. A fixture with one round value
# would have passed on the unfixed compiler.
#
# `reduced` is the cost of agreement rather than a win: 2rem displays as 32em,
# because a compiled target holds the record and has no spelling to prefer.
#
# `zero` pins the shape nothing else reaches: a value carrying no magnitude at
# all prints in the first declared base, since 0rem and 0px are one value.

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:time"

unit tick {
    tk
}

component main ui.node {
    var mix ui.measurement = 3px + 2em
    var reduced ui.measurement = 2rem
    var zero ui.measurement = 1em - 1em
    var ticks tick = 4tk
    var half time.duration = 500ms
    var over time.duration = 500ms + 600ms
    var sMix = ""
    var sReduced = ""
    var sZero = ""
    var sTicks = ""
    var sHalf = ""
    var sOver = ""

    effect(@mount {
        sMix = "{mix}"
        sReduced = "{reduced}"
        sZero = "{zero}"
        sTicks = "{ticks}"
        sHalf = "{half}"
        sOver = "{over}"
    })

    ui.text(value="{mix} {half}")
}

// Two independent bases have no single number, so the value displays as the
// sum it would have been written as.
func testAMultiBaseValueSumsItsBases(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.sMix == "3px + 2em")
}

func testAReducedSuffixDisplaysInItsBase(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.sReduced == "32em")
}

func testAnEmptyValueTakesTheFirstBase(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.sZero == "0px")
}

func testASingleBaseValueCarriesItsSuffix(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.sTicks == "4tk")
}

// 500 is the value Go's own time.Duration.String agreed on; 1100 is the one
// it did not, printing `1.1s` for a unit whose declared base is ms.
func testADurationDisplaysInMilliseconds(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.sHalf == "500ms")
    t.assert(c.sOver == "1100ms")
}

ui.window {
    main
}
-- testrun/bubbletea/go/app.sngl/main/1 --
